title: Rice, brown and wild, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Brown and wild rice are whole grains that retain the bran and germ, making them rich in fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals. When cooked with added fat (oil, butter, or other fats) the energy density increases and the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins improves.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wild rice (Zizania) is not a true rice but a grass species, yet it is marketed as rice because of its similar flavor and texture.
Brown rice keeps the bran layer, giving it a lower glycemic index than white rice.
Wild rice contains higher levels of antioxidants compared with most common rice varieties.
Cooking rice with a small amount of fat enhances mouthfeel and makes the dish more satiating.
In Japan, wild rice is traditionally used in festive dishes and sushi.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nervous system health, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is important for protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Beneficial fats and antioxidants help lower LDL cholesterol and protect blood vessels.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: Added fat raises the calorie content, providing a good energy source for active individuals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the added fat, the dish can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Arsenic presence
items.content: Brown rice can accumulate trace amounts of arsenic from soil; rinsing thoroughly and rotating with other grains reduces exposure.

items.title: Fat allergies
items.content: People with allergies to specific oils should choose alternative fats that do not trigger reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice as a side dish, add it to salads, soups, or pilafs. Use 1–2 tablespoons of oil, butter, or another fat during cooking to enhance flavor and nutrient absorption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with added fat should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3–4 days.
